pool.text: A historic building was constructed that is now among the city's oldest survivors.
Mexico gained independence and subsequently established a local military presence.
A federal garrison and quartermaster depot named the Post of Albuquerque began operating.
Confederate troops under General Henry Hopkins Sibley occupied the community for a month.
Old Albuquerque High School was established as the municipality's first public high school.
The Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railroad arrived and bypassed the traditional Plaza.
The initial travelers driving along Route 66 appeared within the municipality.
John Gaw Meem served as the architect for the University of New Mexico commission.
Route 66 was realigned to follow a more direct east-west path along Central Avenue.
A United States Air Force bomber carrying a nuclear weapon crashed into a nearby mountain.
A military aircraft accidentally dropped a nuclear bomb near the landing area.
The New Mexico Arts and Crafts Fair held its inaugural annual nonprofit exhibition.
Passage of the Arroyo Flood Control Act enabled concrete channel construction.
The Old Main Library building officially received official landmark recognition.
City and county governments established the joint Albuquerque/Bernalillo County Library System.
The Bernalillo County Metropolitan Detention Center opened its doors for operations.
The municipality celebrated its tricentennial with diverse cultural events.
The local government opened the inaugural Bicycle Boulevard along Silver Avenue.
A BioScience Center opened in Uptown Albuquerque as a private incubator.
The state-funded Bioscience Authority was established to promote local industry development.
